Duplicate check: before and after PR #1673

Local test, 2 Nov 2026. 8 contributors, one synthetic Amazon order export each. Old code = 7b74446d0 (#1672); new code = fa4e72cec (main, includes #1673).

Result

#Role1. Old code, originals2. Old code, after tampering3. New code, ids fully regenerated4. New code, dates and ids changed
1–4Untouched originalspassnot re-runnot re-runpass unchanged
5Edited copy of #1passpass missedpass missedfail matches #1, 100%
6Edited copy of #2passpass missedpass missedfail matches #2, 100%

8Edited copy of #4passpass missedpass missedfail matches #4, 100%

The old check misses every edited copy. The new check catches all four, and names the exact source submission. It also leaves the four untouched submissions passing.

How the copies were made

Each copy keeps the source's products, categories, quantities, prices and statuses. On every row it shifts the date and time by 11 days 3 h 17 min, replaces the order id and changes the buyer email. Only the CSV header is byte-identical to the source (1 of 301 lines).

Round 1 regenerated the whole order id (834-8059932-5375139 → 319-4173337-1924317). Round 2 kept the 3-digit prefix and changed only the long parts (834-7832130-9809677). Files are in data/.

Finding: regenerating the whole order id gets past the new check (round 1). The masked view replaces runs of 5+ digits, dates, times, emails and long hex ids. It deliberately keeps short numbers because they look like amounts and counts. So the id's 3-digit prefix survives masking: the copy and its source then share 0 of 300 masked lines, and the edited-copy check scores 0.0039. Anyone who regenerates ids wholesale, rather than editing only the long digits, is not caught.

Notes on the setup

Submissions went through the real browser-upload API: plan, PUT to MinIO, complete. Tampering overwrote each copy's stored export in MinIO, followed by an admin Re-run checks; the files were not uploaded again.

#1–#4 were not re-run after the copies existed. That matches production: a source is checked when it arrives, before any copy exists. The check compares every pair both ways, so re-running a source now would also flag it, as an edited copy of its own copy.

Local-only changes for the test: redaction off on the project (the local redaction runner fails on a MinIO token error), min_apps set to 1, and the authorship LLM check disabled.
